provenance.demand_census: Census 2011 village totals at exact-name matched PMGSY-weighted centroids (22 of 52 villages have a defensible point)
provenance.structures: 3,859 unverified road/water intersection candidates; the allocation uses the 30 highest measured solo-loss candidates

assumed.condition: Uniform{1,2,3} = Fair/Poor/Severe per structure, drawn from the build seed
assumed.age_years: Uniform{5..40} per structure, drawn from the build seed
assumed.structure_type: mapped from the unverified candidate class (see TYPE_FROM_CANDIDATE_CLASS)
assumed.outage_days: placeholder register defaults by structure type
assumed.repair_effects: placeholder register defaults (no Indian inspection history)
assumed.costs: placeholder Schedule of Rates until a PWD reply is ingested
assumed.rainfall: lognormal monsoon ratio, mean 0.0 and sigma 0.4 on the daily loss model

instance.selection_rule: 30 highest measured solo-loss route-carrying crossing candidates (population_hours_lost measured on PMGSY habitations, in crossing_solo_criticality.csv), one candidate per road edge

baseline_equivalence.note: Identical at some budgets but not all: the comparators' identity is budget-specific, so the panel reports worst-first only at its own budget and the per-budget record is kept in `by_budget`.

practice_vs_chance.note: Condition-first beats random by a small absolute margin while spending less, and is nominally worse per crore because of that lower spend. Either reading leaves the practice baseline close to chance relative to the additive policy's gain.

inspection_value.note: Expected gain is the mean objective improvement over the three condition states when that one structure's condition is known; an upper bound because structures are resolved one at a time and the other 29 stay at their assumed state.

equity.note: Benefit is the plan's expected failure-probability reduction per funded structure, split across habitations by that structure's solo-loss share; a first-order attribution, not a re-solve of the joint network.

spend_matched.note: Budgets are per simulated year; the two-year horizon makes the planned total twice the per-year figure. Emergency restoration is reported but not equalised: it is a consequence of failure, not an allocation choice.

precision.note: The 8-scenario row reproduces the reporting panel. TOST rejects equivalence only when both one-sided tests reject; otherwise the reading is 'not distinguishable, and underpowered to claim equivalence at this margin'. required_n is the paired scenario count a TOST at that margin would need at 80% power, so it is a design statement about this estimator.

heuristics.note: All rules buy the condition-appropriate intervention, so the comparison is about the ranking signal. Road-class priority is a declared ordering of OSM highway classes, not measured traffic: the district has no link counts.

variants.selection: mapped evidence only: OSM bridge tag, then snapping offset, then measured loss; no consequence measure drives the order

reordered by measured school solo loss on the same candidate edges

equity_cost.note: Objective weight is (median population / habitation population) ** exponent. Exponent 0 reproduces the reported population-weighted plan; higher exponents count small habitations more heavily. Benefit per habitation is a first-order attribution of each asset's measured solo loss, not a joint re-solve. The Gini is computed over habitations that receive any benefit, matching the reported equity block.

plan.note: Two-period additive schedule: one path per asset, year-0 spend capped at the annual budget, two-year spend capped at twice it (unspent money carries forward). Deterioration is the rounded expectation of the fitted transition matrix; loss uses the optimizer's mean rainfall sample. Emergency repairs and network coupling are not in the model and are supplied by the simulator when the schedule is replayed.

schedule.note: The receding-horizon additive policy re-solves each year at the state it reached, so it already adapts; what it lacks is lookahead and budget carryover. This comparison isolates those two additions. The schedule is solved on a deterministic expected-deterioration path, so it is a scheduling exercise, not an observed maintenance plan.

solver.note: HiGHS is asked for the optimum with no time limit. A zero or absent gap means the additive baseline is solved to optimality for its own linear surrogate; it says nothing about the non-additive objective.
